title: The status LADDER is described as workspace-configured but is a constant: composition.ts passes defaultTaskLifecyclePolicy and no workspace section sets it
description:
Found by QCLI-325's review round 2 (opum-control review seq 8416) as a residual: the paused status is now documented as fixed, but the surrounding prose still calls the status LADDER workspace-configured.

MEASURED, code + experiment, on the dev build (quest 0.13.0, 2026-10-11):
- CODE. src/cli/composition.ts:135-146 createTaskService -- the SOLE CLI composition root -- passes `defaultTaskLifecyclePolicy` (src/application/tasks/tasks.ts:260, a constant alias of defaultLifecyclePolicy). src/application/workspaces/workspaces.ts:34-42 WorkspaceConfiguration carries name, taskIdPrefix, agentSkillSource and taskVocabulary -- no lifecycle or status section. (taskVocabulary is the TYPE/PRIORITY vocabulary, not the status ladder.)
- EXPERIMENT. A fresh workspace with `statuses = [...]` appended to .quest/workspace.toml in FOUR spellings (top level, [tasks], [tasks.lifecycle], [lifecycle]) leaves `task status-flow` reporting statuses ["To Do","In Progress","Done"] in every case -- unchanged.

THE FALSE PROSE, three sites that read as a promise of a workspace status ladder:
- src/application/command-help.ts -- task status-flow opens "Print the configured task status set";
- src/application/command-help.ts -- doctor's summary says "the configured ladder";
- src/application/agents/guides.ts -- "the configured task status set and terminal statuses".

This is the same class QCLI-325 fixed for the paused STATUS, on the ladder rather than the paused literal. Ruling 570 A made only pausedStatus fixed, so the ladder needs its own decision (document as fixed, or make it configurable); it is recorded here as a wording exploit of a capability that does not exist. Filed by the quest-cli worker at team-lead instruction; UNSTAMPED.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The three status-ladder prose sites state the real behaviour: the ladder is fixed by defaultTaskLifecyclePolicy and is not workspace-configurable (or, if it is made configurable, the prose and a test follow)
